Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with acute
right shoulder pain, restricted range of motion, and difficulty with overhead
reaching. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported force of the crash,
and the clinical picture fits the type of trauma described. Over the course of care,
the patient completed 24 visits, consisting of physical therapy, range-of-motion and
strengthening exercises, and periodic re-evaluation. Treatment continued somewhat
longer than is typical for this presentation, largely to address persistent stiffness
and gradual functinoal gains. On examination, some findings, including limited active
elevation and tenderness over the rotator cuff region, support the reported injury,
while other tests, such as neurological screening and stability assessment, remained
within normal limits. The patient reports no prior injury or treatment to this
shoulder. Billing records reflect no duplicate or repeated charges for services.
Current status is improving, with ongoing home exercise and follow-up as needed.
